messages.subject: Dynamic use of checkboxInput()
parts:
I just begin with shiny and I am impressed by the possibilities. But of course I have some problems... here the first one:
I have a data frame (example df.example with columns ref1, separation (a factor) and name) that I would like to use as a guide to build a series of checkboxInput() within a wellPanel().
Now the only solution I found is to code the different checkboxInput() in "hard":
wellPanel(
          p(strong(em(levels(df.example$separation)[1]))),
          checkboxInput(paste0("c",df.example$ref1[1]), paste0("name=", df.example$name[1]), FALSE),
          checkboxInput(paste0("c",df.example$ref1[2]), paste0("name=", df.example$name[2]), FALSE),
          p(strong(em(levels(df.example$separation)[2]))),
          checkboxInput(paste0("c",df.example$ref1[3]), paste0("name=", df.example$name[3]), FALSE),
          checkboxInput(paste0("c",df.example$ref1[4]), paste0("name=", df.example$name[4]), FALSE),
          checkboxInput(paste0("c",df.example$ref1[5]), paste0("name=", df.example$name[5]), FALSE)
)

As the data frame could change, it would be must better if I could create a dynamic version of this code but I fail to find the way to do.

Thanks a lot,

Marc

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Dynamic use of checkboxInput()
parts:
I think what you want in this case is a checkboxGroupInput instead.
But if you insist on creating a list of individual checkboxInput then
you could do it this way:

wellPanel(
p(strong(em(levels(df.example$separation)[1]))),
mapply(function(id, name) {
checkboxInput(paste0("c", id), paste0("name=", name))
}, df.example$ref1, df.example$name, SIMPLIFY=FALSE)
)
